dataset_note: These educational examples use simulated responses that may contain inaccurate claims and are not factual advice. Citation records link to genuine sources; evidence previews are prepared summaries, not direct quotations. This prototype does not use a live AI model, live web retrieval, or automatic fact-checking.

examples.question: Does regular exercise improve sleep quality?
examples.simulated_answer: Regular exercise can improve sleep quality in people with insomnia.

citations.source_title: Exercise can improve sleep quality: a systematic review and meta-analysis
citations.evidence_preview: A systematic review of nine studies involving 557 participants found improvements in reported sleep quality following exercise interventions, although the quality of the evidence was limited.

examples.question: Does caffeine permanently improve memory?
examples.simulated_answer: Caffeine permanently improves memory in all adults.

citations.evidence_preview: Caffeine stimulates the central nervous system. Moderate doses can increase alertness and reduce sleepiness.

examples.question: Do houseplants improve indoor air quality?
examples.simulated_answer: Houseplants significantly improve indoor air quality in most homes.

citations.source_title: Investigation of simultaneous volatile organic compound removal by indoor plants using solid phase microextraction-gas chromatography-mass spectrometry
citations.evidence_preview: Researchers used a sealed experimental chamber to investigate the removal of eight volatile organic compounds by five species of houseplants.
